problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$-3{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}+12x-12y=12?$

feedback.problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$-{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}+12x+24y=-9?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}+12x+24y & =-9 \\ 3{y}^{2}+24y-{x}^{2}+12x & =-9 \\ 3[{y}^{2}+8y]-[{x}^{2}-12x] & =-9 \\ 3[(y+4)^{2}-16]-[(x-6)^{2}-36] & =-9 \\ 3(y+4)^{2}-48-(x-6)^{2}+36 & =-9 \\ 3(y+4)^{2}-(x-6)^{2} & =-9+48-36 \\ 3(y+4)^{2}-(x-6)^{2} & =3 \\ (y+4)^{2}-\frac{(x-6)^{2}}{3} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-(-4))^{2}}{{1}^{2}}-\frac{(x-6)^{2}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center is $(6,-4).$
